factors.label: Pitot probe blockage
factors.description: Pitot probes blocked by ice, insects, covers or debris, or unheated, corrupting airspeed sensing.

factors.label: Static port blockage
factors.description: Static ports obstructed, corrupting altitude, airspeed and vertical speed indications.

factors.label: Unreliable airspeed indication
factors.description: Cockpit airspeed indications inconsistent with actual airspeed, typically following pitot or static failures.

factors.label: Spurious overspeed warning
factors.description: Overspeed warning triggered by erroneous airspeed data rather than actual overspeed.

factors.label: Angle-of-attack sensor failure
factors.description: An angle-of-attack vane provided erroneous data to flight control or warning systems.

factors.label: MCAS activation
factors.description: The 737 MAX Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System commanded repeated nose-down stabilizer trim from a single erroneous AoA input.

factors.label: ADIRU data fault
factors.description: An air data inertial reference unit output corrupted data, driving spurious flight control or warning responses.

factors.label: Radio altimeter failure
factors.description: A radio altimeter provided erroneous height, typically feeding automation with a false landing condition.

factors.label: Erroneous engine indication
factors.description: Engine instrumentation read incorrectly, typically from iced probes, leading the crew or autothrottle to set wrong thrust.

factors.label: Autopilot disconnect
factors.description: The autopilot disconnected, handing the aircraft to the crew, often at the start of an upset.

factors.label: Flight control law degradation
factors.description: Fly-by-wire protections were lost or degraded, removing stall or attitude protections the crew may have relied on.

factors.label: Autothrottle mode confusion
factors.description: The crew misunderstood what the autothrottle or autothrust was doing, allowing thrust to remain at idle or an inappropriate setting.

factors.label: Automation mode confusion
factors.description: The crew's mental model of the automation's active modes diverged from the actual state.

factors.label: Automation dependency and manual skill erosion
factors.description: Habitual reliance on automation degraded manual flying proficiency or willingness to fly manually.

factors.label: Aerodynamic stall
factors.description: The wing exceeded its critical angle of attack and lost lift.

factors.label: Stall or upset misdiagnosed
factors.description: The crew misidentified the aircraft's state: not recognizing a stall, or treating another condition as a stall or overspeed.

factors.label: Inappropriate stall recovery
factors.description: The crew's control inputs during a stall or approach to stall deepened it, typically nose-up inputs or overriding the stick pusher.

factors.label: Stick shaker or pusher activation
factors.description: The stall warning stick shaker or stall protection stick pusher activated.

factors.label: Dual sidestick input
factors.description: Both pilots made simultaneous sidestick inputs without clear transfer of control.

factors.label: Inappropriate flight control input
factors.description: Control inputs outside what the situation required, including excessive or oscillatory inputs.

factors.label: Startle and surprise
factors.description: A sudden unexpected event degraded the crew's cognitive performance during the critical seconds after it.

factors.label: Loss of situational awareness
factors.description: The crew lost track of the aircraft's position, energy state, configuration or trajectory.

factors.label: Inadequate monitoring and cross-check
factors.description: The pilot monitoring did not detect or call out deviations in speed, altitude, configuration or flight path.

factors.label: CRM breakdown
factors.description: Crew coordination, communication, or challenge-and-response failed, including steep authority gradients.

factors.label: Sterile cockpit violation
factors.description: Non-essential conversation or activity during a critical phase of flight distracted the crew.

factors.label: Procedural non-compliance
factors.description: The crew did not follow a checklist, standard operating procedure or limitation.

factors.label: Fatigue
factors.description: Crew fatigue from duty time, sleep loss, commuting or circadian disruption degraded performance.

factors.label: Inadequate training
factors.description: The crew had not been trained, or trained adequately, for the situation encountered.

factors.label: Low experience on type or in role
factors.description: Limited experience on aircraft type or in the crew role contributed.

factors.label: Spatial disorientation
factors.description: The crew lost accurate perception of the aircraft's attitude or motion.

factors.label: Somatogravic illusion
factors.description: Longitudinal acceleration was perceived as a pitch-up, prompting a nose-down input.

factors.label: Visual illusion
factors.description: Terrain, lighting or weather created a misleading visual picture of the approach path.

factors.label: Pilot incapacitation
factors.description: A pilot became unable to perform duties from medical or environmental causes.

factors.label: Deliberate act by crew
factors.description: Investigators concluded the accident resulted from an intentional act by a crew member.

factors.label: Unstabilized approach
factors.description: The approach was outside stabilized approach criteria and was continued.

factors.label: Go-around not initiated
factors.description: A go-around was warranted but not initiated, or initiated too late.

factors.label: Long landing or touchdown beyond zone
factors.description: The aircraft touched down beyond the touchdown zone, consuming runway needed to stop.

factors.label: Tailwind on landing
factors.description: A tailwind component increased groundspeed and landing distance.

factors.label: Wet or contaminated runway
factors.description: Water, snow or ice on the runway degraded braking.

factors.label: Delayed deceleration devices
factors.description: Reverse thrust, spoilers or brakes were applied late or not at all after touchdown.

factors.label: Runway overrun
factors.description: The aircraft departed the runway end or side.

factors.label: Runway incursion
factors.description: An aircraft or vehicle was on a runway without authorization or in conflict with another.

factors.label: Wrong runway or taxiway used
factors.description: The crew took off or landed on a runway or taxiway other than the one cleared.

factors.label: Takeoff without clearance
factors.description: The crew began the takeoff roll without a valid takeoff clearance.

factors.label: ATC communication breakdown
factors.description: Communication between ATC and the crew failed through ambiguity, blocked transmissions, language or non-standard phraseology.

factors.label: ATC staffing and workload
factors.description: Controller workload, staffing or fatigue degraded ATC performance.

factors.label: TCAS RA versus ATC instruction conflict
factors.description: A TCAS resolution advisory conflicted with an ATC instruction and the crew followed ATC.

factors.label: Midair collision
factors.description: Two aircraft collided in flight.

factors.label: Ground collision
factors.description: The aircraft collided with another aircraft or vehicle on the ground.

factors.label: Surface surveillance unavailable
factors.description: ATC had no functioning surface surveillance to detect the conflict.

factors.label: Airport signage, markings or lighting deficiency
factors.description: Airport signage, markings, lighting or layout contributed to crew or ATC error.

factors.label: Controlled flight into terrain
factors.description: An airworthy aircraft under crew control was flown into terrain, water or an obstacle.

factors.label: Loss of control in flight
factors.description: The crew lost control of the aircraft in flight.

factors.label: Inadequate response to GPWS/EGPWS
factors.description: A ground proximity warning was ignored, responded to late, or was not installed or effective.

factors.label: Minimum safe altitude warning inhibited
factors.description: The ATC minimum safe altitude warning system was inhibited or ineffective.

factors.label: Navigation or lateral path error
factors.description: The crew misjudged position or descended below safe altitude through navigation error.

factors.label: Altimeter setting error
factors.description: An incorrect altimeter setting or altimeter reading error caused an altitude misjudgment.

factors.label: Descent below minimums
factors.description: The crew descended below the applicable minimum altitude without required visual references.

factors.label: Low visibility
factors.description: Fog, cloud, darkness or precipitation restricted visual references.

factors.label: Dark night conditions
factors.description: Darkness removed external visual references.

factors.label: Thunderstorm or convective weather
factors.description: Thunderstorms, convective activity or associated turbulence and precipitation contributed.

factors.label: Windshear or microburst
factors.description: A sudden change in wind velocity along the flight path exceeded the aircraft's performance margin.

factors.label: Airframe ice accretion
factors.description: Ice accreted on the airframe, degrading lift and control.

factors.label: Inadequate ground de-icing or anti-ice use
factors.description: Ground de-icing was inadequate, or airframe or engine anti-ice systems were not selected on.

factors.label: High-altitude ice crystals
factors.description: Ice crystals at altitude affected probes or engines beyond certification envelopes.

factors.label: Fuel system icing
factors.description: Ice released in the fuel system restricted fuel flow to the engines.

factors.label: Volcanic ash encounter
factors.description: The aircraft flew through volcanic ash, damaging engines or systems.

factors.label: Bird strike
factors.description: Birds struck the aircraft or were ingested by engines.

factors.label: Engine failure or power loss
factors.description: One or more engines lost power.

factors.label: All-engine power loss
factors.description: All engines lost thrust, forcing a glide.

factors.label: Uncontained engine failure
factors.description: An engine rotor failure ejected high-energy fragments that damaged the aircraft.

factors.label: Wrong engine shut down
factors.description: The crew shut down the functioning engine instead of the failed one.

factors.label: Wrong lever or control selected
factors.description: The crew operated the wrong lever, switch or control.

factors.label: Fuel exhaustion
factors.description: All usable fuel was consumed.

factors.label: Fuel starvation
factors.description: Fuel was on board but did not reach the engines because of mismanagement or system failure.

factors.label: Fuel leak
factors.description: A fuel line or tank leaked in flight.

factors.label: Fuel quantity calculation error
factors.description: The fuel on board was miscalculated, misindicated or misplanned.

factors.label: Fuel tank explosion
factors.description: Flammable vapour in a fuel tank ignited.

factors.label: Electrical wiring failure
factors.description: Electrical wiring chafed, arced or short-circuited.

factors.label: Flammable cabin or insulation material
factors.description: Cabin or insulation materials sustained fire propagation.

factors.label: In-flight fire
factors.description: Fire or smoke developed in flight.

factors.label: Cargo compartment fire
factors.description: Fire started in a cargo compartment, often from undeclared or improperly packaged dangerous goods.

factors.label: Delayed diversion or lengthy smoke checklist
factors.description: The crew delayed landing to complete procedures or dump fuel while a fire developed.

factors.label: Explosive or rapid decompression
factors.description: The cabin lost pressure suddenly.

factors.label: Cabin pressurization not maintained
factors.description: The cabin failed to pressurize or gradually depressurized without crew recognition.

factors.label: Hypoxia
factors.description: Insufficient oxygen incapacitated occupants.

factors.label: Cargo door failure
factors.description: A cargo door opened or failed in flight.

factors.label: Structural failure in flight
factors.description: Primary structure failed in flight.

factors.label: Metal fatigue
factors.description: Cyclic loading produced cracks that led to failure.

factors.label: Pressure bulkhead failure
factors.description: A pressure bulkhead failed, typically from an improper repair.

factors.label: Total hydraulic failure
factors.description: Hydraulic power to flight controls was lost.

factors.label: Flight control system failure
factors.description: A flight control surface or its actuation failed or jammed.

factors.label: Rudder hardover or reversal
factors.description: The rudder moved uncommanded or opposite to input.

factors.label: Horizontal stabilizer trim failure
factors.description: The horizontal stabilizer trim system failed, jammed or ran away.

factors.label: In-flight thrust reverser deployment
factors.description: A thrust reverser deployed in flight.

factors.label: Windshield failure
factors.description: A cockpit windshield failed in flight.

factors.label: Landing gear failure or collapse
factors.description: The landing gear failed, collapsed or did not extend.

factors.label: Maintenance error
factors.description: A maintenance action was performed incorrectly, or a required action was omitted.

factors.label: Inadequate lubrication or wear inspection
factors.description: Insufficient lubrication or wear checks allowed a component to wear to failure.

factors.label: Inadequate inspection program
factors.description: Inspection intervals or methods were insufficient to detect the defect.

factors.label: Weight and balance error
factors.description: The aircraft was loaded outside limits, or its weight or balance was miscalculated.

factors.label: Takeoff performance data error
factors.description: Erroneous takeoff weight or performance data produced insufficient thrust or wrong speeds.

factors.label: Takeoff configuration error
factors.description: The aircraft took off without flaps or slats set, typically with the takeoff warning system inoperative.

factors.label: Tail strike
factors.description: The tail contacted the runway on takeoff or landing.

factors.label: Hard landing or bounced landing
factors.description: A high vertical speed or bounced touchdown damaged the aircraft or led to loss of control.

factors.label: Ditching
factors.description: The aircraft was intentionally landed on water.

factors.label: Post-impact fire
factors.description: Fire following impact affected survivability.

factors.label: Evacuation or survivability deficiency
factors.description: Evacuation or survival was hindered by equipment, procedure or behaviour.

factors.label: Design deficiency
factors.description: The aircraft or system design had a flaw or assumption that contributed.

factors.label: Certification shortfall
factors.description: The certification process failed to identify or address the hazard.

factors.label: Warning or alerting deficiency
factors.description: A warning was absent, inhibited, ambiguous or easily confused with another.

factors.label: Regulatory oversight deficiency
factors.description: The regulator's surveillance or rule-making was insufficient.

factors.label: Operator safety culture or management
factors.description: Operator management, culture, hiring or pressure contributed.

factors.label: Manufacturer communication or documentation failure
factors.description: The manufacturer failed to inform operators or crews of a system behaviour or hazard.

factors.label: Known defect not resolved
factors.description: A defect or hazard had been reported previously but not corrected before the accident.

factors.label: Hostile or criminal act
factors.description: The accident resulted from a bomb, hijacking, missile or sabotage.

factors.label: Successful emergency landing
factors.description: The crew landed the aircraft with no or few fatalities despite a serious failure.

factors.label: Checklist or procedure design flaw
factors.description: The published checklist or procedure was inadequate, ambiguous or too long for the situation.

factors.label: High workload and task saturation
factors.description: Simultaneous demands exceeded the crew's capacity.

factors.label: Excessive speed for phase
factors.description: The aircraft was flown faster than appropriate for the phase or configuration.

factors.label: Low energy state on approach
factors.description: Airspeed decayed below the target during approach without correction.

factors.label: Reduced control authority
factors.description: The crew lacked sufficient control authority to recover.
